texts.preamble: State Of Gujarat vs Jethalal Pritamdas Khetani on 11 February, 2026 R/Cr.Ra/518/2013 Judgmen In The High Court Of Gujarat At Ahmedabad R/Criminal Revision Application (Against Order Passed By Subordinate Court) No. 518 of 2013 For Approval And Signature: Honourable Mr.Justice P. M. Raval ========================================================== Approved for Reporting Yes ========================================================== State Of Gujarat & Anr. Versus Jethalal Pritamdas Khetani & Anr. ========================================================== Appearance: Mr. Rohan Raval, App for the Applicant(s) No. 1,2 Rule Served for the Respondent(s) No. 1,2 ========================================================== Coram:Honourable Mr.Justice P. M. Raval Date : 11/02/2026 Oral Judgment
texts.facts: The facts of the prosecution, as revealed from the record, in nutshell, are as follows:- 2.1. That original accused No.1 was the distributor, No.2 was the owner of Santosh Milk House, No.3, is the nominee of the manufacturing firm and No.4 is the firm. The original complainant - Food Inspector had visited the shop of respondent - original accused No.2 and purchased the sample of Narmada Pasteurinzed Standard Milk. After doing certain formalities of packing sealing, drawn the Panchnama and send the sample to the Public Analyst for analysis. The Public Analyst reported that the sample does not conform to the standards and provisions of the Act and Rules as the percentage of milk fat was less than the prescribed as also mild solid not fat was found less than the prescribed. After getting sanction, the complainant - Food Inspector has lodged the complaint. Hence, the present revision application by the State.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr. Rohan Raval would contend that : 3.1. The learned Judge ought to have considered the evidence of complainant - C P Gohil, who has been examined at Exhibit 10. Witness has deposed in his testimony that he had followed all the necessary procedure prescribed under the law and after obtaining necessary permission from the Court, he had filed a complaint. The learned Judge ought to have appreciated the evidence of the complainant in true and letter spirit, as the complainant in his evidence before the Court has very categorically stated about the procedure complied with by him while drawing of the sample in the presence of Panch witness and State Of Gujarat vs Jethalal Pritamdas Khetani on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22130339/ 2 thereafter sending one sample out of three to the Public Analyst and on receipt of the report of Public Analyst, the sanction was obtained to file a case. As such no lacuna is found in the procedure carried out by the complainant. 3.2. The learned Judge ought to have considered the fact that report of Public Analyst indicates that the sample does not conform to the standards and provisions fo the Act and Rules as the percentage of milk fat was less than the prescribed as also milk solid not fat was NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/518/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/02/2026 undefined also found less than the prescribed. 3.3. It ought to have been appreciated that there is no reason to disbelieve the report of the Public Analyst because as per the report there is no evidence with regard to tampering with the sample and therefore the benefit of non-examination of the person who conducted the analysis of the sample would not be given to the accused. 3.4. The learned Judge has erroneously come to the conclusion by not believing the report of the Public Analyst which states that sample of the milk does not confirm to the standard of the provisions laid down under the provisions of PFA Rules, 1955. 3.5. The learned Judge has erred in holding that the evidence with regard to the utensils in which the sample was drawn is not dry and clean and thereby procedure laid down under Rule 14 of the Act is violated and benefit of that was given to the respondent-accused. In the case of Sanjaysinh Ramrao Chavan v. Dattatray Gulabrao Phalke, reported in (2015) 3 SCC 123, wherein in paragraph 14, it is held that: State Of Gujarat vs Jethalal Pritamdas Khetani on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22130339/ 3 "14. ... Unless the finding of the court, whose decision is sought to be revised, is shown to be perverse or untenable in law or is grossly NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/518/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/02/2026 undefined erroneous or glaringly unreasonable or where the decision is based on no material or where the material facts are wholly ignored or where the judicial discretion is exercised arbitrarily or capriciously, the courts may not interfere with the decision in exercise of their revisional jurisdiction." 6.1. Further, in the case of Southern Sales & Services v. Sauermilch Design and Handels GmbH, reported in (2008) 14 SCC 457, it is held that "... Revisional Court will not interfere even if a wrong order is passed by a court having jurisdiction, in the absence of a jurisdictional error".
